value.tagline: Skura's first season in Philadelphia ends with Super Bowl CXLVII, a record debut for Bones Crawford, a third OPOY for Vyncint Heath and two new Hall of Famers.

articles.headline: Philadelphia Rises: Skura Takes the Eagles to the Super Bowl CXLVII Title
articles.dek: In his first season in Philadelphia, Dorren Skura led the Eagles to a 14-2-1 record, past Atlanta and Green Bay, and to a 40-22 win over the Broncos.
body: A new city, a new roster and the same ending. Dorren Skura left Atlanta after five straight championships, took over the Philadelphia Eagles, and won again. The Eagles finished the regular season 14-2-1, beat the Falcons and the Packers at home in the playoffs, and handled the Denver Broncos 40-22 in Super Bowl CXLVII.

It is the Eagles' first title since Y4, when they also beat Denver, 36-28. In between, Philadelphia lost five Super Bowls, the last of them a 46-8 defeat by Skura's own Jets in Y82. The coach who handed the Eagles that loss has now delivered the parade.

The quarterback was a newcomer. Bones Crawford, on his first card, threw for 5,922 yards and 69 touchdowns, then was named Super Bowl MVP. His favorite targets were two receivers built for volume. Vyncint Heath, acquired from Atlanta, caught 140 passes for 2,204 yards and 28 touchdowns and won his third Offensive Player of the Year award. Kaulani Rahman, another new card, added 2,247 yards on 124 catches.

The road ran straight through Skura's old house. Atlanta, still led by Ryland Maxwell, reached the playoffs and met the Eagles in Philadelphia, and the Eagles ended the Falcons' title run there. Green Bay, with Most Valuable Player Solomon Toohill, fell the same way a round later.

Two losses, one tie and a championship in the first year of a rebuild is a remarkable debut. For Skura it is something more familiar: one more season that ended with a trophy, this time in a third city.

articles.headline: Bones Crawford Arrives With 69 Touchdown Passes and a Super Bowl MVP
articles.dek: The Eagles quarterback put up one of the great debut cards in league history: 5,922 yards in 20 games.
body: Few quarterbacks on a card have opened a career like Bones Crawford. In his first 20 games he threw for 5,922 yards and 69 touchdowns, and he capped the season as the Super Bowl MVP in Philadelphia's win over Denver.

The profile is aggressive. Crawford averaged 296 passing yards and more than three touchdown passes a game, a quarterback who attacks downfield and trusts his receivers to win the ball, and the cost was 26 interceptions. On an offense with Vyncint Heath and Kaulani Rahman, that bargain paid off week after week.

The market has not caught up yet. His card opens at an overall of 62, because overall rewards a long career, but his skill grade is already an S. If the next seasons look anything like this one, that overall will not stay low for long.

articles.headline: Heath for Adam: The Receiver Swap That Shaped the Season
articles.dek: Philadelphia sent Apollo Adam to Atlanta for Vyncint Heath, and Heath answered with a third Offensive Player of the Year award.
body: The biggest trade of the offseason sent one star receiver each way between Skura's old club and his new one. Apollo Adam, the two-time Offensive Player of the Year, went from Philadelphia to Atlanta. Vyncint Heath, "Starscream", came the other way.

Heath made the deal look lopsided. He caught 140 passes for 2,204 yards and 28 touchdowns, won his third Offensive Player of the Year award and added his seventh ring. His card's overall climbed from 86 to 90, and its value rose 115%.

Adam was good, not great, in his first Atlanta season. He caught 71 passes for 1,123 yards and 20 touchdowns, and he appeared in 18 of the Falcons' 19 games, so he missed time; a knock may have played a part, as may a new offense. His card's value still rose 73%, and the market clearly expects the best of his career to be ahead of him. The Eagles took the win in the playoff meeting, but this trade will be judged over several seasons, not one.

articles.headline: Spector Scores 35 in Houston After the Ogbah Trade
articles.dek: The Eagles moved Siran Spector to the Texans for Gerrit Ogbah. Both backs had good years, and both teams can claim the deal.
body: Philadelphia's other offseason swap was in the backfield. Siran Spector went to Houston and Gerrit Ogbah came to the Eagles, and the results split neatly along the lines of what each club needed.

Spector was a touchdown machine for the Texans. He ran for 1,533 yards and 35 touchdowns in 19 games and caught 17 passes, and his skill grade rose from a B to an A minus. Houston did not get back to the final, but it found a back who finishes drives.

Ogbah gave the champions balance rather than headlines. He ran for 1,051 yards and 12 touchdowns, caught 27 passes for 185 yards and 4 more scores, and collected the first ring of his career in Super Bowl CXLVII. With Bones Crawford throwing for 5,922 yards, the Eagles did not need a workhorse. They needed a back who kept defenses honest, and Ogbah did that for 20 games.

articles.headline: The Falcons Run Ends Where the Coach Went
articles.dek: Atlanta still had Ryland Maxwell and a playoff team. It did not have Skura, and its run of titles ended in Philadelphia.
body: For five seasons the Falcons were the league's standard, champions every year from Y83 through Y87. Then the coach left, and the first team to stop Atlanta was the one he went to coach.

The talent did not disappear. Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,403 yards and 23 touchdowns in 19 games, his card's overall rose to 97 and his Career Legacy climbed to 8,057. Apollo Adam arrived from Philadelphia and scored 20 touchdowns. The Falcons made the playoffs and traveled to Philadelphia with a real chance.

They lost there, and the drop in Maxwell's numbers tells part of the story. A year after his record 2,670-yard season he gained a little more than half that total. A defense that no longer had to fear the threat of a historic season may have keyed on him; age and a new offensive rhythm may also have played a part.
Atlanta remains dangerous. But for the first time since Y82, Atlanta finished a season without the trophy.

articles.headline: Toohill Wins a Second MVP and Brooker Takes Defensive Honors
articles.dek: Green Bay collected two of the season's biggest awards before the Eagles ended its year in the playoffs.
body: Solomon Toohill is now a two-time Most Valuable Player. The Packers quarterback threw for 4,522 yards and 43 touchdowns against only 4 interceptions in 20 games, the second straight season he paired heavy volume with almost no mistakes. His card's value jumped 345%.

His teammate in the secondary had a breakout of his own. Jamon Brooker made 259 tackles and intercepted 6 passes and was named Defensive Player of the Year, adding to the Rookie of the Year award already on his card. His skill grade rose to an A and his card's value climbed 241%.

The Packers had the league's best regular-season quarterback and its best defender, and they still came up one round short again, beaten by Philadelphia in the playoffs. Green Bay has the pieces. It keeps running into Dorren Skura.

articles.headline: McClain and Orzech: Two One-Club Linemen Enter the Hall
articles.dek: The 49ers and Cowboys defensive linemen both crossed Career Legacy 7,500, and McClain finished the season one tackle from a record.
body: The Y88 Hall of Fame class belongs to the trenches. Aqib McClain of the 49ers and Keion Orzech of the Cowboys, two defensive linemen who have spent their whole careers with one club, both pushed their Career Legacy past 7,500.

McClain is the more remarkable case. He finished Y88 with 1,363 career tackles, one fewer than Lloyd Queen's 1,364, the most by any defensive lineman on a card, and he had made them at a faster pace. He added 97 tackles this season, and his card's value more than doubled, up 113%.

Orzech came into the league as Rookie of the Year and by the end of Y88 had made 1,296 tackles in 271 games. His signature is unusual for a lineman: 6 career interceptions, more than any of the great tacklers at his position.
Neither had won a ring. Both now have a place in the Hall.

articles.headline: Diggs Passes 20,000 Yards and Takes the Rushing Touchdown Lead
articles.dek: The Jaguars back moved past Trequan Jensen for the most rushing touchdowns on a card and closed in on Ikarras for yards.
body: Danny Diggs has been chasing names for years. In Y88 he caught one of them. The Jaguars back scored 22 rushing touchdowns, which lifted his career total to 393 and past Trequan Jensen's 388, the most by any back on a card.

He also ran for 1,139 yards and went past 20,000 career rushing yards. Only Rondale Ikarras, "The Prodigal Son", had more, with 23,178, and Diggs ended Y88 2,853 yards behind him. At his recent pace that is two to three more full seasons, so the chase is real but not close.
Diggs has done it without a ring or an individual award. His card's overall rose to 95. For a player still waiting on a title, the record book is becoming the trophy case.

articles.headline: A Champion Built on New Cards
articles.dek: Rahman, Shaheed and Brock joined Crawford as first-time cards on the title team, and Cairo Colbert arrived with a long career already behind him.
body: Philadelphia won with a roster full of unfamiliar names. Beyond Bones Crawford, the Eagles fielded three more players on their first cards. Kaulani Rahman caught 124 passes for 2,247 yards. Kenyon Shaheed, a tight end, caught 63 for 967 yards and 14 touchdowns in 18 of the Eagles' 20 games, so he missed time; injury may have been a factor. Akiem Brock made 60 blocks in 20 games, 3.0 a game, at the time the best career rate of any lineman on a card.
All of them won a ring in their first season, and Brock's skill grade opens at an S.

The pool also gained a veteran it had never tracked. Cairo Colbert arrived with 228 games, 16,993 rushing yards and 288 rushing touchdowns, a career long enough that his first card already carries an overall of 85. Tight ends Rodger Samuel and Treyvon Scott, linebacker Khaleke Hyder and defensive lineman Deshone Bello also joined the market with long careers behind them.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Around the league in Y88.
body: Kahzin Heath threw for 3,870 yards and 30 touchdowns in 21 games and took the Broncos to Super Bowl CXLVII.
Ty Lock of the Giants threw 38 touchdown passes and only 1 interception.
Kalif Suh of the Jets added 3 sacks to reach 24, and his card's overall rose from 87 to 90.
Linval Laulile of the Steelers intercepted 5 passes, and his card's value rose 219%.
Trequan Roberts won his third ring with the Eagles but appeared in 17 of their 20 games, missing time that may have included an injury.
Dwayne Skura made 169 tackles in his first Eagles season and collected his second ring.
Chazz McCray of the Buccaneers made 234 tackles, and his card's overall climbed from 84 to 87.

didYouKnow.text: Bones Crawford threw 69 touchdown passes in the first 20 games of his career, more than three a game.
Akiem Brock averaged 3.0 blocks a game in his first 20 games, at the time the best career rate of any lineman on a card.
Aqib McClain finished Y88 with 1,363 career tackles, one behind Lloyd Queen for the most by a defensive lineman.
The Eagles beat the Broncos in both of their Super Bowl wins, 36-28 in Y4 and 40-22 in Y88.

value.tagline: A record season on the ground, a second straight title in Atlanta won with key pieces missing time, and two new names in the Hall of Fame.

articles.headline: Atlanta Does It Again
articles.dek: The Falcons went 13-3-1 and held off the Broncos 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, carried by a record season from Ryland Maxwell and two first-year players who left with rings.
body: The Falcons are champions again. Atlanta finished the regular season 13-3-1, survived a four-point final against the Denver Broncos, 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, and gave Dorren Skura a third straight title: one with the Jets, now two with the Falcons. A roster that was torn apart and rebuilt after the first ring simply did it again.

This one was won on the ground. Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,272 yards and 27 touchdowns, the best rushing season the record board has ever shown, and finished the job as Super Bowl MVP. He played all 20 games of the run and now owns 4 rings in 97 career games.

The passing game belonged to a newcomer. Orlando Larienne, in his first season, threw for 3,485 yards and 41 touchdowns and left with a ring. He appeared in only 15 of the 20 games, and a team that also saw Vyncint Heath miss time still found a way. Heath, the receiver they call "Starscream", caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards anyway and won a second Offensive Player of the Year award.

Up front, Calais Ham made 49 blocks in his first season and has a ring to show for it. Shawn Milne, who came from Tampa Bay in the trade that sent Shareef London the other way, won the first of his career, and Chance Woodrum now has 5.

Up the coast, the old club had a milestone of its own. Malakai Sawyer ran for 1,551 yards for the Jets and crossed into the Hall of Fame, the only member of its Y84 class. In Los Angeles, the Rams' Von Horsted crossed the same line, though he has since fallen out of the Hall. The Falcons kept winning.

articles.headline: Maxwell Runs Into the Record Book
articles.dek: 2,272 rushing yards in one season, a Super Bowl MVP and a fourth ring before his hundredth game.
body: No back on the record board had ever had a season like it. Ryland Maxwell carried the Falcons for 2,272 yards in Y84, the new mark for the best rushing season, and added 27 rushing touchdowns plus 4 more as a receiver. He did it in every one of Atlanta's 20 games, the one constant on a roster that had to cover for missing pieces elsewhere.

It was a jump even from the year he won Offensive Player of the Year, when he ran for 1,919. His career now reads 7,705 rushing yards and 102 rushing touchdowns in 97 games, and the season pushed him past 100 rushing scores.

The market noticed. His card rose from an overall of 67 to 75 and from a C+ grade to B+, and its value went from 20 to 112. With 4 rings and a Super Bowl MVP before his hundredth game, Maxwell has stopped being the back who followed the coach from New York. He is the reason Atlanta keeps winning.

articles.headline: A Title Won Short-Handed
articles.dek: Orlando Larienne played 15 of Atlanta's 20 games and Vyncint Heath played 18. The champions won anyway.
body: The Falcons' two most productive passing pieces were not always on the field. Orlando Larienne, a first-year quarterback, appeared in 15 of the club's 20 games, missing 5. Injury may have played a part; so may the usual caution with a newcomer on a new team. When he played, he was devastating: 41 touchdowns against 13 interceptions, better than three scores for every pick. His card opened in the A+ tier.

Vyncint Heath missed 2 games, a year after playing all 21 of Atlanta's first title run. Whether he was slowed by injury or simply by the wear of back-to-back deep seasons, the absence barely showed in the numbers. In 18 games he caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards and 22 touchdowns, 18.6 yards a catch, and took his second Offensive Player of the Year award. His card climbed into the S tier, its overall from 70 to 77.
Both finished with rings. For a team that had to keep winning with a starter or a star in street clothes, that may be the most telling number of all.

articles.headline: Green Bay Finds Its Back
articles.dek: Angelo Moton ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns and was named Rookie of the Year for the Packers.
body: Angelo Moton did not ease into the league. In his first 20 games for the Packers he ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns, and the Rookie of the Year award went to Green Bay. His 31 rushing scores matched what Malakai Sawyer, a new Hall of Famer, managed for the Jets in the same season.
There is one thing to clean up. Moton also put the ball on the ground more often than a back of his talent should, the kind of habit that decides playoff games.

He had help. Solomon Toohill played all 20 games at quarterback and threw for 3,845 yards and 41 touchdowns with 5 interceptions, his card rising from an overall of 66 to 70. Toohill already has a ring from Green Bay's 44-6 win over the Chiefs in Super Bowl CXXXVIII. With a back like this behind him, the Packers have reason to think about another.

articles.headline: Sawyer Stands Alone in the Y84 Hall Class
articles.dek: A back who keeps running for the Jets crossed Career Legacy 7,000. A Rams safety who never left Los Angeles crossed it too, but his place did not last.
body: The Y84 class has 1 member, and it is Malakai Sawyer. Sawyer, in his second season back with the Jets, ran for 1,551 yards and 31 touchdowns in 19 games, passed 15,000 career rushing yards and reached a Career Legacy of 7,101. He ended Y84 with 16,436 rushing yards and 299 rushing touchdowns in 243 games, 2 rings and 2 Offensive Player of the Year awards.

Von Horsted got there too, one tackle at a time. A Ram since Y70 and nothing else, he played all 17 games, made 231 tackles, 13.6 a game, and intercepted 2 passes. That lifted his career to 2,658 tackles and 33 interceptions in 254 games and his Career Legacy from 6,833 to 7,345. His card's value rose from 3,118 to 4,806. His Career Legacy has since slipped below the mark the Hall asks its earlier members to hold, and he is no longer part of the class.
Sawyer's résumé is rings and records. Horsted's is a Defensive Player of the Year award and a body of work built entirely in one uniform. Only one of them is still in the Hall.

articles.headline: Record Watch: A Dead Heat for Fourth
articles.dek: Von Horsted caught Dan Mosley at 2,658 career tackles, 204 short of Mose Junior, with K'Lavon Settle closing behind them.
body: The career tackle mark belongs to Mose Junior at 2,862. Jayon Queen is second at 2,838 and Karl Deane third at 2,681, and behind them the chase is a tie. Von Horsted's 231 tackles for the Rams brought him to 2,658, the exact total Dan Mosley of the Lions already had. Both are 204 short. Junior's card wears the Rams colours too, so Horsted would be chasing a club legend as well as a league one.
K'Lavon Settle is the name coming up fastest. The 49ers defensive back made 189 tackles and picked off 5 passes, passed 2,500 for his career and now sits at 2,545, 317 short, with an A+ grade.
Settle is also climbing the interception list with 32, 8 behind Jayon Queen's 40. Mosley, at 37, is 3 away from that one.
In the backfield, Derrick Myrick has 347 rushing touchdowns, 41 behind Trequan Jensen's 388.

articles.headline: Long Careers, Late Introductions
articles.dek: Vic Cannon in Los Angeles, Terron Stidham in Baltimore and Marvell Rodgers in Tennessee joined the card pool with decades of work already behind them.
body: Vic Cannon has been a Charger since Y65, and his card finally caught up with him: 336 games, 59,531 passing yards, 561 touchdown passes and a Rookie of the Year award, but no ring. The man he most resembles is Kirk Lenoir, the Jaguars lifer, who has 564 touchdown passes, 3 more than Cannon, and also no ring. Cannon's card opened at an overall of 85.

Terron Stidham has spent every season since Y74 in the Ravens secondary, with 1,980 tackles and 21 interceptions in 178 games after winning Rookie of the Year. Marvell Rodgers has done the same for the Titans since Y77: 1,637 tackles in 139 games, 11.8 a game, and an 80 overall. In Detroit, Travon Swaim, another former Rookie of the Year, has 597 tackles in 54 games beside Dan Mosley.
None of the four has a ring. All of them now have a card.

articles.headline: The Jets Hand the Ball to a Rookie
articles.dek: Jimmy Tillery was intercepted only 4 times in his first season. Ty Lock, the old starter, is a Giant now.
body: The club Skura left behind went with youth at quarterback. Jimmy Tillery played all 19 of the Jets' games in his first season and threw for 3,392 yards and 27 touchdowns, with only 4 interceptions. He was not explosive, but he was careful, and careful kept the Jets in games.

He had a Hall of Famer behind him in Malakai Sawyer and a familiar target in Jaylen Conklin, the tight end they call "Takeoff", who caught 85 passes for 513 yards. Kalif Suh played all 19 games on defense.

Across town, Ty Lock is a Giant now, traded there from the Jets in the multi-team deal before Y83. He played 18 games and threw for 3,204 yards and 24 touchdowns with 2 interceptions. Lock owns 2 rings and 2 MVP awards. Tillery has a long way to go to match that, but the start was clean.

articles.headline: Life After Atlanta
articles.dek: Brandon Jaclyde, Shareef London and Perrion Randall left the champions after one season. All three spent Y84 watching their old club win again.
body: The Falcons traded away three pieces of their first title team, and none of them got a second ring. Brandon Jaclyde, the reigning Most Valuable Player, went to Miami and threw for 2,807 yards and 26 touchdowns with only 2 interceptions in 17 games for the Dolphins. Solid, but a long way from the 56 touchdowns he threw as a Falcon.

Shareef London's road ran from the Bears to Atlanta in the multi-team deal before Y83, then on to Tampa Bay in the trade for Shawn Milne. He caught 61 passes for 464 yards and 5 scores with the Buccaneers, 7.6 yards a catch. Milne, meanwhile, collected the ring.

Perrion Randall played 17 games for the Seahawks and was credited with 16 blocks. His card actually climbed, its overall from 66 to 74, even as his grade fell from the S tier to B+. For all three, Atlanta was a single season, a single ring, and then a view from somewhere else.

articles.headline: Denver Meets Skura, and Loses, Again
articles.dek: Four Super Bowls against the Broncos, four wins, with three different clubs across 68 seasons.
body: The Broncos have now reached the final against Dorren Skura four times and lost every one. The first came in Y16, a 22-16 win with the Commanders. Two more followed with the Buccaneers, 46-11 in Y23 and 38-16 in Y25. Then nothing for nearly six decades, until Atlanta beat Denver 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII.

This was the closest of the four by a distance. The first three were decided by six points or more, two of them by more than three touchdowns. Denver had a four-point game and a tight end with a long memory: D.C Paradis, who has 995 career catches, played all 20 games of the Broncos' run and is now five catches short of a thousand.
For Skura it is a rivalry measured in eras. The Commanders, the Buccaneers dynasty and now the Falcons have all taken their turn, and the Broncos are still waiting for their first win.

Spector ran for 1,194 yards and 23 touchdowns and now has 116 rushing scores in 75 games.
Spencer Daniels of the Jaguars passed 200 games and 5,000 receiving yards, but his 51 catches went for 216 yards, 4.2 a catch.
Kane Van Oxley caught 60 passes for the Bears at 6.4 yards a catch; the card's value still rose from 1,906 to 2,150.
Danny Diggs and Matthew Waynes both passed 300 career rushing touchdowns, and both finished the season at exactly 306.

Corey Ivey, Wise's Ravens teammate, added 1,382 rushing yards and now has 19,508 for his career.
